Description: Detected a Generic API Key, potentially exposing access to various services and sensitive operations.
Author: leofishman
Message:
Port the seller side of quebracho/x402: verify, screen, claim, settle

First code of the port. A device can now charge for a request end to end on
any POSIX host, and every step is checked against the PHP library itself:

- quebracho-x402 (no_std core): one-spelling field rules, the EIP-3009
  TransferWithAuthorization digest (type hashes computed, never typed in),
  low-s ecrecover, EvmExact::verify with the x402 v2 reason codes, the
  payment key, PAYMENT-* headers, offer matching, OFAC screening on unless
  turned off by name, and the sale itself (X402Middleware + Sale): pay on
  delivery or upfront, ledger replay, pending lookups, stop switch.
- quebracho-x402-ofac: OFAC's SDN list as shipped by the PHP library.
- quebracho-x402-qnx: std adapters. FileLedger keeps PHP's file layout (PHP
  reads a Rust-written ledger) and adds fsync before rename; StopFile;
  SystemClock that is not trusted below a floor (threat T6).
- conformance/: export.sh runs the PHP library in Docker and writes the
  vectors (keccak, field, signer, digest, recover, evm_exact) and 34 scripted
  sale scenarios; the Rust tests must answer exactly as PHP did.

Deliberate differences, documented in seller.rs: a ledger is required (no
claims-only mode), no deferred address lookups, no ChainFacilitator
reference callback, and an unreliable clock refuses new payments (503).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Description: Detected a Generic API Key, potentially exposing access to various services and sensitive operations.
Author: leofishman
Message:
Test every path of the core against PHP; fix what the tests found

Coverage (cargo-llvm-cov) showed which paths no test ran. Each one now has a
test, and where PHP is the source of truth the expected answer comes from
PHP:

- evm_exact.json grows to 99 cases: offers and echoes of every JSON type,
  to pin PHP's (string), (int) and empty() casts. They found that Rust gave
  invalid_payment_requirements where PHP gives a bad signature (an array
  name is "Array" in PHP), and refused a sloppy chain id PHP reads ("eip155:
  084532"). php.rs now casts exactly as PHP 8.3 does, values checked with
  php -r and kept in its unit test; the chain id is read as PHP reads it.
- settlement.json: receipt normalization, settle answers, verify reasons,
  offer matching, payment keys and mock mode, from PHP's Settlement.
- sale.json grows to 55 scenarios (stop pressed mid-sale, handlers failing
  after the settle, ledger failing on the second read, lookups that throw,
  every stored state). Big bodies are stored as hash and length.
- Property tests (proptest): no panic and no admission for random headers
  and payments, field rules against their definition, uint256, dates,
  lists. One found that floats did not survive a JSON round trip: serde_json
  now uses float_roundtrip.
- Seller-internal tests for races between the two ledger reads and for the
  guards that keep a sale from releasing what it does not hold.

Dead code removed: hex32, and the branches php_string can no longer reach.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
